caseno: Appeal from Original Order No. 258 of 2001
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam with Shishir Kanti Majumder —For the Appellant. 

M Enayetur Rahim Advocate—For the Respondents.
parties:
Samar Kanti Das Gupta ------ Appellant
vs
Bangladesh Bar Council & another ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 25. Generally a charge of criminal or quasi criminal nature is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt, but as Denning, J (as he then was) in Miller vs Minister of Pension (1947 2 All ER 372), emphasised, "beyond reasonable doubt" does not mean "beyond shadow of doubt," and as he (by then a Lord Justice) pronounced in Bater vs Bater, (1950 2 All ER 458) that standard of proof may fluctuate depending on what is at stake. Hence, in the prevalence of dreadful soaring in the occurrences of professional misconduct, the weight of proof in disciplinary proceedings against advocates and, of course, members of similar professional bodies, may desirably be relaxed to an acceptable proportion. But proving an allegation with a lighter burden of proof is one thing, and adducing no evidence at all, is quite another. In the instant case, there was simply no evidence to substantiate the charges recorded in the indictment. It is to be added that an advocate instructed to simply draft a bainanama undertakes no suo motu obligation to conduct search on the title to the property, and nothing in the Bar Council rules proscribes drafting of bainanama.
